value: wild elephants moved further away from the trial location when seismic tracks contained human-generated noise (white noise and combined tracks)
method: field playback of seismic tracks through a buried speaker to wild elephant families; distance moved scored before, during and after a 2-min treatment against silent control periods
conditions: Wild elephants in the Samburu and Buffalo Springs National Reserves, Kenya (Methods: 'the seismic tracks were played to wild elephants within the Samburu and Buffalo Springs National Reserves in Kenya'). Three treatments: elephant-generated seismic recordings (Ele), white noise (WN) and a combined track (Ele&WN). Each 6-min track: 2 min of silence, 2 min of treatment, 2 min of silence (silent periods are the controls). Stimulus at the animal: speaker on average 17.3 m (SD 3.9 m, n = 32) from the focal individual; Methods print that this propagation distance 'gives maximum amplitude levels at ca less than 1E-5 m s-1' (velocity, below elephant footstep and car seismic amplitudes). n: 16 independent families or sub-families, 7 receiving all three treatments; focal trials 10 Ele, 11 WN, 11 Ele&WN (reader summary). Results: distance moved away increased significantly in WN and Ele&WN over the experimental periods (p < 0.01 for both; Friedman chi2(2) = 9.29 and 10); no significant response to the elephant-generated (Ele) treatment alone, which the authors discuss. Head scanning and freezing also rose in the human-noise treatments. Seismic sensitivity at the animal is an amplitude ceiling, not a threshold.
